issues.reason: An existential clause reifies no eventuality, and `Time` attaches only to an event witness or an event-denoting noun, so "now" has no licensed anchor here (the swim events sit inside the rule and are not what "now" modifies); the instruction set's own direction in the parallel case is to leave an unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it.

Real that the connective form is defined over two reified eventualities and neither slot holds one, so the sentence's causal claim — about the penguins' coming to exist — is only approximated; overstated as a defect, because `ThanksTo` is the surface multiword preposition CamelCase-joined per the stated convention (not a coined synonym head) and the atom is true of the sentence in territory the reviewer itself records as uncovered.

gaps_confirmed: causal PP with an NP complement ("thanks to / because of / due to <NP>"): the connective atom requires two reified eventualities, and the entity-attached surface-preposition licence is scoped to position, origin and noun/adjective complements, so this construction has no licensed route
new_gaps: an existential clause ("there are now penguins …") reifies no eventuality, so a time adverb modifying the existence has no anchor — the copular-with-time-modifier reification trigger needs a property state to reify and an existential supplies none

a relational / classifying adjective modifier (`genetic`, `dental`, `nasal`) — the modifier-genus rule enumerates gradable, positional/cardinal and material adjectives only, and its "can it be predicated of the thing?" test is marginal for classifying adjectives
notes: Removing the `ThanksTo` atom would delete stated content with no licensed replacement, so the partial verdict stands without repair. The group witness plus distributing rule correctly avoids claiming penguins in general swim in lava.
